title: Vacuum Ejector

introduction.definition: A steam jet vacuum ejector has no moving parts. Motive steam expands in a converging–diverging nozzle to supersonic speed and low pressure, entraining gas from the suction chamber; the diffuser then slows the mixture and recovers its pressure to the discharge.
key_points: Multi-stage with condensers for deep vacuum
Sensitive to steam pressure and discharge pressure
introduction.summary: A steam jet vacuum ejector has no moving parts. High-pressure motive steam expands through a converging–diverging nozzle to very high (supersonic) velocity and low pressure, which entrains gas from the suction chamber. In the diffuser the mixture slows down and its pressure rises to the discharge pressure. Several ejectors in series with condensers reach deep vacuum.

alignment: Install diffuser outlet to condenser without pipe strain; keep nozzle concentric.
piping: Supply dry, superheated motive steam at design pressure with a strainer and separator.
commissioning: Check rotation direction with the coupling disconnected.
Fill lubricant to the correct level and grade.
Start unloaded where possible; record vibration, temperatures, current and pressures as a baseline.

video_tutorials.title: Vacuum Ejector — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Vacuum Ejector.
A steam jet vacuum ejector has no moving parts.

Motive steam expands in a converging–diverging nozzle to supersonic speed and low pressure, entraining gas from the suction chamber; the diffuser then slows the mixture and recovers its pressure to the discharge.
Typical applications include refinery vacuum distillation; steam-turbine condenser air removal; evaporators and crystallisers; deodorisers (edible oil).

The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Motive Steam Chest & Inlet Flange, Converging–Diverging Steam Nozzle, Suction Chamber & Suction Flange (load connection), Diffuser (converging inlet, throat, diverging outlet).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Vacuum Ejector — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Vacuum Ejector.
Check motive steam pressure and suction pressure.
Inspect and clean the nozzle throat.
Inspect diffuser for erosion; replace nozzle.
Watch for loss of vacuum ("break"): suction pressure jumps up. Common cause: low steam pressure, high discharge pressure, worn nozzle.
Watch for air in-leakage: higher load, poor vacuum. Common cause: leaking flanges/process.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
